Definition: of uncertain affinity; a reed (the plant or its stem, or that of a similar plant); by implication, a pen:--pen, reed.
BiblicalUsage: Kalamos is a reed — the stalk by the water, the measuring rod, the mock sceptre. Jesus asks what the crowds went out to see, a reed shaken with the wind; He says the bruised reed He will not break; the soldiers put a reed in His right hand and mocked Him; and John is given a reed like unto a rod to measure the temple.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the reed is the whole gospel in one picture: the weakest thing, shaken by the wind, is the thing Christ will not break — and the same reed that mocked Him becomes the rod that measures His temple. A bruised reed is still a reed, and He does not break it.
